newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy in fresh bid to revive Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy in fresh bid to revive Mideast talks.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross will launch a fresh bid on Wednesday to revive stalled Middle East peace talks in a mission overshadowed by a corruption scandal that could threaten Israel's government.

Ross's efforts appeared to get a boost even before he landed in Israel as Maltese officials said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy were meeting in Malta during a Euro-Mediterranean conference.
It was the first high-level Israel-PLO meeting since peace talks were halted last month over Israeli settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. But officials on both sides ruled out a compromise.

"We made it clear to them that Jabal Abu Ghneim is a red line. We can't accept it, it contradicts the peace process," Palestinian Authority member Hanan Ashrawi told Reuters, referring to the hill where Israeli bulldozers were working.
Israel sealed off the West Bank early on Wednesday, citing intelligence warnings of a possible attack like one on March 21 when a Palestinian bomber killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe.

But dominating Israeli media were reports that police had recommended corruption charges against men close to Netanyahu. A 995-page report was given on Tuesday to state prosecutors who will decide within days whether to issue indictments.

Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said the alleged suspects, including Justice Minister Tzahi Hanegbi, the director-general of Netanyahu's office, Avigdor Lieberman, and key coalition legislator Aryeh Deri were "without blemish".
"I am certain the state attorney's conclusions will prove that my feeling is right," he told Israel Radio.

Police had been looking into the ill-fated appointment of an attorney general in January. Israel's Channel One television alleged that Deri, an ultraorthodox legislator already on trial for corruption, had pushed candidate Roni Bar-On for the job in hopes of winning a plea bargain.
All those questioned have denied any wrongdoing. Bar-On himself quit hours after being appointed amid criticism he was professionally unfit for the job.
Reports that government officials would be charged prompted calls for Netanyahu to step down. At least two ministers in his cabinet have said if the allegations are true, the government must fall.
Netanyahu would not comment until the prosecutors made their decision.
"The prime minister is dealing with diplomatic matters now...in the afternoon he will meet with the U.S. envoy Dennis Ross," said Bazak.
Arabs have battled Israeli troops almost daily in the West Bank since construction of 6,500 homes for Jews began in East Jerusalem, land captured by Israel in 1967.
Israel has accused Arafat of sanctioning violence by Islamic groups against the Jewish state and says a PLO crack down on militants must be the first step in restoring peace talks.

"We made it quite clear that the talks cannot be revived on a substantive level before we see a very substantial change in the attitude and actions of the Palestinian Authority on the issue of terrorism and violence," Netanyahu's communication's director, David Bar-Illan, told Reuters.

Asked if Israel in response would freeze construction in East Jerusalem, he said: "Anything that compares bombs with bulldozers is an obscenity and an insult to the intelligence of every decent human being and we're not going to discuss it."
